articles.title: Charges Filed Months After Sheriff's Office Announced Suspicious Bathroom Activity at Little League Opening Day, No Arrest Made
articles.description: Richard Allen Lehman, 58, of Hollywood, is facing 18 misdemeanor charges after investigators alleged he secretly recorded six people, including two juvenile males, inside a men's restroom at Chancellors Run Regional Park in Great Mills during Little League Opening Day activities in April 2026. The charges were not filed until August 17, 2026, more than four months after the alleged incident. A criminal summons was issued for Lehman rather than an arrest warrant, and as of 2:20 p.m. on August 19, 2026, the available information did not show that the summons had been served. Lehman is charged with six counts of Peeping Tom, six counts of conducting visual surveillance in a private place with prurient intent, and six counts of using a camera to conduct visual surveillance of a person's private area with prurient intent. The St. Mary's County Sheriff's Office had publicly acknowledged the investigation months before charges were filed. In an April 11, 2026 news release, the agency said deputies working security for St. Mary's Little League Opening Day ceremonies responded at approximately 9 a.m. to reports of a man engaging in suspicious behavior inside a restroom at Chancellors Run Regional Park in Great Mills. The Sheriff's Office said one person was detained and that the Criminal Investigations Division was handling the investigation. The agency asked anyone who witnessed suspicious activity or had additional information to contact Detective Andrew Burgess. The release did not identify the person who was detained. The St. Mary's County Sheriff's Office initially reported the incident occurred during Little League Opening Day on April 11, 2026. St. Mary's Little League's official schedule also confirms Opening Day was April 11. However, the filings against Lehman list April 13, 2026, as the offense date for all 18 charges. The reason for the discrepancy is not explained in the filings. According to allegations later filed by the St. Mary's County Sheriff's Office, patrol officers were working a part-time security assignment at Chancellors Run Regional Park for the 2026 Little League Opening Day ceremonies when an off-duty Maryland State Police master trooper used the men's restroom and entered the second toilet stall. The dividers between the stalls did not extend completely to the ground. While inside the stall, the trooper noticed a person in the first stall with his pants or shorts pulled down and a cellphone hanging from his left pocket. The trooper believed the phone had been deliberately positioned and angled toward the adjoining stall in a manner consistent with secretly recording someone. While inside, the trooper noticed a person in the first stall with his pants or shorts pulled down and a cellphone hanging from his left pocket. The trooper believed the phone had been deliberately positioned and angled toward the adjoining stall in a manner consistent with secretly recording someone. The trooper reported first noticing the same person in the restroom shortly after arriving at the park. About an hour later, he escorted a juvenile male into the restroom. After the juvenile left the stall, the trooper said he could see the same person's pants and cellphone in nearly the same position he had observed earlier. When the man exited the restroom, the trooper identified himself as a police officer. Authorities said the man was identified through his Maryland driver's license as Lehman. Patrol officers asked Lehman whether he had any cellphones on him. According to investigators, Lehman removed a blue Apple iPhone from his pocket. The trooper told officers that was not the phone he had seen hanging from the pocket inside the restroom. Lehman then retrieved a black Motorola Android smartphone from another pocket, according to the allegations. Officers seized both phones. St. Mary's County Sheriff's Office D/Cpl. David M. Lawrence later sought a search warrant for the Motorola phone. The warrant was authorized by Judge A. Lorenzini. Lawrence reported that investigators recovered numerous videos from the Motorola that allegedly had been recorded from inside the men's restroom at Chancellors Run Regional Park. Investigators identified six alleged victims, including four adults and two juvenile males. Their names are being withheld to protect their privacy. Authorities alleged that none of them knew they were being recorded or had consented to the recordings. One of the juvenile victims was allegedly captured in four separate videos. Investigators said the recordings showed the alleged victims using the restroom with various parts of their bodies exposed. The two juvenile males were allegedly recorded while sitting on a toilet, with the side of their buttocks visible. The six Peeping Tom charges allege Lehman conducted visual surveillance of another person in a private place without that person's consent. Each count carries a listed maximum penalty of 30 days in jail, a $1,000 fine, or both. The six private-place surveillance charges allege that Lehman conducted visual surveillance with prurient intent and without consent. The six additional camera-surveillance charges allege that he used a camera to record a person's private area with prurient intent and without consent. Each of those counts carries a listed maximum penalty of one year in jail, a $2,500 fine, or both.

articles.title: Man charged with burglary and voyeurism after allegedly trespassing into high school bathroom, stealing items
articles.description: LONE PEAK, Utah (ABC4) -- A man has been arrested and charged with burglary, voyeurism, and lewdness after he allegedly entered a high school, stole several items, walked into the women's bathroom, and urinated outside. Justin Lane Hopkins, 54, was charged with burglary (a third-degree felony), voyeurism, theft with prior convictions, possession of a dangerous weapon by a restricted person, criminal trespass, lewdness, and littering. According to charging documents, on Aug. 12, Lone Peak Police received a call of a potential trespass at Lone Peak High School. The alleged trespass happened two days earlier, and police claim video footage showed Hopkins entering the school building two separate times on the same day. Reportedly, Hopkins took several items from the building, including an hourglass, a book-shaped box, a can of soda, and a drawstring backpack. Police say the value of the items totaled approximately $500. Then, Hopkins allegedly opened an exterior door of the school and urinated, and shortly after that, he held the door open for someone to enter the building. Police also say that Hopkins entered a women's restroom inside the school twice while events were occurring and while there were people inside the school. Hopkins had previously been trespassed from the school, and signs throughout the building stated that visitors need to check in at the front office. After reviewing the footage, police found Hopkins in an encampment at Highland Glen Park. He allegedly admitted to entering the high school and taking items, and officers found the stolen items in his encampment. They also located a knife, and Hopkins reportedly acknowledged that he was on probation and that he wasn't supposed to have a knife. Police also noticed garbage around the camp, which was in a public park. Hopkins has a history of numerous drug-related convictions dating back to 2012. Most recently, he pleaded guilty to possession of a controlled substance in January 2025. Hopkins is being held in the Utah County Jail with bail. He had his initial court appearance on Monday, Aug. 17, and he has a waiver hearing scheduled for Aug. 26.

articles.title: Convicted sex offender accused of recording women in changing rooms
articles.description: A Tennessee man reviously convicted of secretly recording women and children in restrooms and dressing rooms has been charged for similar conduct in Fayette Mall in Lexington, according to court records. Ty Cline, 31, of Oliver Springs, Tennessee, is charged with video voyeurism. Court documents say he secretly recorded a 40-year-old woman in a changing room at the Fayette Mall on July 31.

articles.title: Hidden camera found in changing room at Mass General Brigham research lab
articles.description: Boston police are investigating after a device resembling a hidden camera was found in a locker room area at an off-campus Mass General Brigham lab. According to the police report, officers assigned to a paid detail at Brigham and Women's Hospital responded to a radio call shortly after 9 a.m. Wednesday for a hidden camera device that had been found at an off-campus research facility in Roxbury leased by Mass General Brigham. When they arrived, officers spoke with a security officer, who said he had received a radio call from a manager reporting that a hidden camera device had been found inside the shower/changing room area. The security officer took custody of the device and turned it over to police. Officers spoke with managers, who told them the victim was opening the exit door to leave the shower room and enter the laboratory facility when she saw the device, which then fell to the floor. Police detectives responded to the scene, took possession of the device and processed and photographed the scene. The incident remains under investigation. It has not yet been determined if the device was a camera. Mass General Brigham issued a statement, saying: "We are aware that a small device resembling a camera was found in a locker area of an off-campus leased research lab space. We immediately notified the Boston Police Department and are cooperating fully with law enforcement. Out of an abundance of caution, the area was secured and appropriate safety protocols were followed. The space is badge-access only and limited to researchers; patients and other staff do not have access."
